slot_note: re-root after architectures 1 to 4 were spent at stage 4 (no retirement, the author's rule); a fresh world in the ETL objective: a turnpike authority ranks its twelve corridors for its 2027 virtual weigh station contract by the share of five-axle tractor-semitrailers its weigh-in-motion stations weighed over the 80,000-lb gross limit in 2026
niche: a turnpike authority's twelve corridors ranked for 2027 virtual weigh station installations by each corridor's 2026 share of five-axle tractor-semitrailers over the 80,000-lb gross limit, weighed by piezoelectric and bending-plate weigh-in-motion stations whose calibrations differ, each station's level read off its loaded tractors' steer axles against the scale houses' static tickets
answer: Equip Cole Hollow, Elk Ferry, Garnet Ridge, Jessup Fork and Kettle Run with the 2027 virtual weigh stations (11, 16, 21, 11 and 11 per cent of their weighed class 9 trucks over 80,000 lb on the static basis, against Dunmere's 7).
analyst_test: A strong analyst who parses the authority's per-vehicle WIM records, keeps the five-axle tractor-semitrailers and reads the program's rules correctly counts each corridor's share over 80,000 lb from the weights as recorded and fills the five installations with corridors whose stations read high; carrying each station's weights to the scale houses' static level through its loaded tractors' steer axles fills a different five.
domain_test: General statistics, so the swap is of the method: the deciding quantity is the share of a measured population above a fixed limit, read through instruments that each carry their own multiplicative bias, the bias measured per instrument on a component whose true size depends only on a coarse state and not on what the limit tests, matched by that state to a reference reading of the same component. In the turnpike's nouns this is the traffic monitoring field's own weigh-in-motion quality control on class 9 steer axles; with another field's nouns the steer axle, the load-state matching and the static scale have nothing to attach to.
layer2_pattern: own:an instrument's multiplicative bias measured on a load-independent component, matched by load state to a static reference, before readings are counted against a limit
layer1: two sensor vendors' per-vehicle exports: the piezoelectric stations' fixed-width records with weights in hundreds of pounds against the bending-plate stations' CSV in kilograms
station controller clocks on local standard time all year against the toll system's UTC timestamps
a controller replacement during 2026 that renumbered one station's lanes
the station-to-corridor list keyed by milepost, with one station re-sited along the road in 2025
records the controller flagged (speed out of range, axle weights not summing to the gross) left in the export
the scale houses' static tickets keyed at the scale, axle weights in pounds and the gross typed separately

spine.entity: one vehicle weighed by one WIM station in one lane
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the layout of a per-vehicle weigh-in-motion record export)

world.org_type: a public turnpike authority operating a toll road

driver: The decisive quantity is the share of a measured population above a fixed limit, read through instruments that each carry their own multiplicative bias; a component of every unit whose true size depends only on a coarse state and not on the quantity the limit tests is read by the same instruments, so its level at each instrument, matched by that state to a reference reading of the same component, measures the instrument's bias, and dividing each reading by it before counting moves the ranking the raw readings give, while matching unlike states moves it again.
driver_concrete: Each corridor's 2026 share of five-axle tractor-semitrailers over the 80,000-lb gross limit is counted from piezoelectric and bending-plate WIM stations whose weights run several per cent high or low; a tractor's steer axle carries its cab and engine and moves only with whether the trailer is loaded, so each station's loaded tractors' steer-axle level against the scale houses' loaded static tickets measures its calibration, and the raw weights and an all-tractor steer calibration each fill the five installations differently from the calibrated weights.
stump: The default path counts each section's class 9 trucks over 80,000 lb on the gross its weigh-in-motion station recorded and equips Brannock, Cole Hollow, Garnet Ridge, Ingram Mill and Jessup Fork; each station reads every axle through its own calibration (Brannock's, Foxbriar's and Ingram Mill's 5 to 7 per cent heavy, Elk Ferry's and Kettle Run's 4 to 5 per cent light), which only its loaded tractors' steer-axle median against the scale houses' loaded static tickets measures, because a loaded tractor's steer axle does not move with the cargo while the tickets are pulled-in heavy trucks and the sections haul different freight.

differentiation.task478: architecture 4 resolved position reports displaced by a direction-dependent latency into distinct entities on surveyed covers; here weights read with a station-level multiplicative bias are counted against a gross limit, the bias read on a load-independent axle matched by load state to static tickets, and nothing is linked or counted as entities
differentiation.task252: task252 calibrates an online analyser's readings against physical verification checks and attributes a movement; here no instrument is ever checked against a known load, and the reference is a component every weighed unit carries
differentiation.task228: task228 ranks the instruments themselves by their own random error, identified from the covariances of three independent series of one unobserved signal; here the instruments are never ranked: the units they weigh are counted against a fixed legal limit after each instrument's systematic multiplicative bias is read on a load-independent component, matched by load state to a static reference

lineage.driver: Each section's potholes per ten lane-miles in March 2027 counts the potholes no camera unit recorded, completed segment by segment as one over the chance that at least one of the distinct installed units that drove the segment found a pothole, the per-unit chance (0.542) read from how often a second unit found a pothole another unit found; a unit records the same potholes on every pass (99.5 per cent of its later days), so a segment its section's patrol pickup drove on seven or more days has had one chance.
lineage.stump: The default path completes the potholes no unit recorded by treating every pass over a segment as an independent chance at the rate a pass re-finds a found pothole (64 per cent of unit-days), which changes nothing on segments driven seven or more times, and designates Carrow Point and Elmscourt only; the rural and outer suburban sections one unit drove hide close to half their potholes, and Fenwick Gap, Thistlebank, Holloway Run, Kestrelton and Norvelle clear the line at 7.08 to 8.29.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-21: reader G (the ninth isolated reader) landed the call by distinct-unit capture-recapture; readers C to H kept ask A's counts and two kept the camera miles

lineage.driver: Distinct entities are counted from repeated positional reports by instruments of unequal accuracy, each instrument's error measured on surveyed control objects, so reports are linked within a tolerance that follows the instrument; any single tolerance either splits a noisy instrument's reports of one entity or merges an accurate instrument's reports of distinct neighbours.
lineage.stump: The default path links the pothole detections into potholes with one milepost tolerance for every unit and designates another set at any tolerance it picks; the street sweepers' older Kerbline units place their reports of one pothole tens of feet apart while the patrol units' reports of neighbouring bridge-deck potholes sit a few yards apart, so only a tolerance set by each unit's error on the surveyed utility covers resolves both.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-21: readers C and D landed the call by folding the sweepers' visibly scattered reports into the precise units' potholes; the camera miles ask leaked to both round 1 readers and was dropped

lineage.driver: A count seen through several instruments is completed by multiple-list recapture, and instruments of one family see the same members while different families see independently, so the occasions are the distinct families that looked at a unit at the cross-family recapture rate, not the instruments; taking every instrument as independent overstates the find rate and completes too little.
lineage.stump: The default path completes pass by pass and designates Carrow Point and Elmscourt; the careful path takes every installed unit as an independent chance at 69.9 per cent and designates five; units of one fleet group record 93.6 per cent of each other's potholes against 54.9 per cent across groups, so the chances are the fleet groups at 54.4 per cent, and Fenwick Gap (6.86) and Kestrelton (7.28) join Holloway Run, Carrow Point, Elmscourt, Thistlebank and Norvelle.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-21: round 2 reader D landed the call and all 14 rates by estimating each fleet group's visibility by maximum likelihood after seeing units of one group agree 93 to 100 per cent; the judge noted a unit-level truncated MLE also landed the seven

lineage.driver: Distinct entities are counted from position reports that each instrument displaces along its direction of travel by its own latency times its speed, so one entity seen in both directions appears as two tight clusters; the latency is calibrated on control objects of surveyed position and each report corrected by its pass's direction and speed before linking, while any single linking distance either splits the two directions or merges close neighbours.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each section's potholes per ten lane-miles counts the distinct potholes its Kerbline detections resolve to after each detection is moved back along its pass by its unit's GPS latency (measured against the asset inventory's surveyed utility covers) times the pass's speed from the telematics traversals, because every phone places what it sees ahead of where it is, northbound to the north and southbound to the south.
lineage.stump: The default path links the pothole detections at one distance and designates Holloway Run, Carrow Point, Elmscourt, Thistlebank and Norvelle at anything from 132 to 410 feet, or a seven with Grisholt and Oxbrae at 54 to 124 feet, because every Kerbline phone places a detection ahead of the pothole along its direction of travel by its own GPS latency times its speed, so on the two-lane roads one pothole seen both ways is two clusters while the bridge decks' neighbouring potholes sit closer than that; each detection moved back by its unit's latency on the surveyed covers at its own pass's speed and direction, the detections designate the seven.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-22 at stage 4: reader F of eight landed the call by fitting each unit's lag from cluster offsets on the pass's signed speed; a displacement proportional to speed is identifiable from the clusters themselves, so the surveyed covers were a convenience
